messages.subject: RAM Allocation during Modelling
parts:
Hi Wallaceans !

While modelling in small areas is efficient and fast, trying to use Wallace in larger areas seems tricky.

I have a large area (Mediterranean and Indopacific) of ~140.000.000 pixels of 1*1km (Maxent GUI run smooth)

All stages of preprocessing work fine and fast at a PC of i7 and 16 GB ram (thus assume that no issue with RAM has to pop up).

Unfortunately, when am going for multiple beta multipliers (e.c 1>5 with 1 unit step) after running MAXENT with L1, LQ1, and H1 - system stop and inform that it cannot allocate vector of 1.2 GB.

Prior opening Wallace i run the > options(java.parameters = "-Xmx12000m") in order to increase the available RAM to MAXENT (but seems that it doesn't work).

How can we solve this issue ?

I have install the development version via Github.

Looiking forward

Dimitris

messages.author: d73691b565754184
messages.subject: Re: RAM Allocation during Modelling
parts:
Hi Dimitris,

I do not see any solution because ENMeval is storing the raster internally for each combination of feature classes and regularization multiplier (also for each partition bin). This problem is not from the java parametrization; it is because your machine cannot handle all the 'huge' rasters of the combinations that you want. I suggest to change your envdata to a lower resolution or run multiple times Wallace by changing the parameters.

Maybe the implementation of 'maxnet' package in the ENMeval (new version) could fix this problem. However, we can not know until maxnet is incorporate in Wallace (~ 1 month).

Let me know if you have other questions. Hopefully, we can help you more next time!

Best,
Gonzalo

messages.subject: Re: RAM Allocation during Modelling
parts:
Hi Dimitris,

Sorry for the late reply. We are working hard in the upcoming version of Wallace (v.1.0.6).

I think that is not necessary to buy more ram. You can run Wallace multiple times with all your combinations (just not include all of them in one run). Then, you can download the tables per session, and select your model once you run all the parameters combinations that you want. Also, maybe you could try to run the models with the maxnet implementation once is released. We are not sure if this will be a better way to handle memory problems but maybe could fix them.

Best,
Gonzalo
